title: SoftTech Engineers Ltd. (NSE: SOFTTECH) — Company Dossier
sector: Information Technology / Application Software (AEC permit automation, GovTech)
archetype: Capitalised-software GovTech with unproven cash conversion
primer: SoftTech Engineers builds software that Indian cities use to approve building plans. FY2026 revenue grew 39.5% to ₹132.9 crore, yet group profit was ₹5.3 crore and free cash flow has been negative every year since FY2019. The business verdict is CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL with KPI health PASS_WITH_WATCH, and new capital is REJECTED at the ₹420.95 verified close (latest print ₹425.90) because the price needs 29-35% revenue growth for five years. Our weighted FY2028E value is ₹369, 13.5% below the latest print. The company is not held, and we would reopen the file if audited FY2027 free cash flow turns positive with collection days under 200, or if the price reaches ₹218-₹242.
holding_rationale: The same-session positions ledger shows no SoftTech shares, so there is no holding to keep, trim or exit and zero shares are to be sold. The new-capital verdict is REJECTED because the price assumes growth and cash conversion beyond management's own plan and the base-case value of ₹299 is below the reference support band. If you wanted exposure anyway, a 5% position would be about 504 shares, 11.2% of an average day's volume, which is a liquidity cost the stop would not cover.

holding_alerts.instruction: Re-run the dossier with the new base case; no purchase is triggered automatically.

holding_alerts.trigger: Q3 FY2027 results (expected February 2027): group pre-tax margin above 10% and orders in hand excluding JNPA above ₹232 crore
holding_alerts.instruction: Use as an early check on the base case and revisit the 30% bear probability.

holding_alerts.trigger: Price falls into the valuation watch band
holding_alerts.instruction: Re-underwrite the business first; the band assumes the ₹299 base case is unchanged. This is an alert, not a broker order.

redeployment_plan.capital_source: Next marginal cash unit; SoftTech is not held, so no sale proceeds are freed by this dossier

destinations.entry_condition: Fund a shortlist name only after a current dossier confirms the evidence and a support entry with at least 1.5:1 reward-to-risk.

destinations.rationale: MapmyIndia, Cyient, Nucleus, Ramco and Datamatics were screened only to test SoftTech's multiple and are not underwritten buy candidates.
destinations.entry_condition: Fund an outside name only after a separate evidence-backed review with a fresh price, support zone and stop.

destinations.recommendation: Retain the entire next marginal unit in cash.
destinations.rationale: SoftTech fails the price test and the timing gate, and no alternative was underwritten in this run, so cash preserves optionality at no cost in risk.
destinations.entry_condition: Reallocate when an equity candidate clears the evidence, valuation and entry hurdles.

horizons.rationale: Timing gate is CAP_REJECTED, volume is balanced (up/down ratio 0.99), turnover is about ₹20 lakh a day and the price is below its 20-day, 50-day and 10-week averages.
Growth and orders are real; audited free cash flow after capitalised development, collection days and credit-loss charges must improve in FY2027.
Return on invested capital is about 4% against a 13% cost of capital, and large-order repeatability beyond JNPA is unproven.

gate_exceptions: Citation check exceptions (as-of age): research record SOFTTECH:fy26_consolidated_cfo describes the year to 31 March 2026 (₹31.26 crore, 3,126.39 lakh consolidated operating cash flow in the FY2026 annual report) and is 226 days older than the 12 November 2026 report date; research record SOFTTECH:ramco_provision_h1_fy24 is ICRA's 8 November 2023 rationale for the Ramco Systems provision, 1,100 days old. Neither is replaceable: audited FY2026 is the latest annual cash-flow statement until FY2027 results (expected May to June 2027), and the Ramco event is a historical case study. Both are used as dated history, not as current values.

The configured reviewer model azure//claude-sonnet-5-5 and red-team model ao-foundry-lc/gpt-6.1-sol were not selected explicitly by the agent runner; both passes ran on the runner's default agent. The independent reviewer returned BLOCK in round 1 (missing as-of exception disclosure, now added above, plus consistency findings, corrected) and REVISE in round 2 on one mechanical figure that was then corrected without a third review, so this report carries BEST_EFFORT_AFTER_REVIEW_LIMIT status and did not receive a reviewer APPROVE. The red team found that the REJECTED verdict holds. Small template fixes were also made to scripts/dossier_builder_template.py and scripts/options_snapshot.py during the run: a duplicated 'NOT HELD' phrase, a currency-neutral 'rupee/dollar' sentence, an RSI-conditional overextension note, and an options-setup note that previously described a 4H turn that the same snapshot did not show.

The market-wide scripts/stage2_scanner.py dashboard scan failed twice for the India filter set: first with RuntimeError 'Could not clear all Stage 2 slicers' and, on one retry, with an AppleScript error 'Can't get tab 9 of item 1 of every window. Invalid index. (-1719)'. The company-specific stock_snapshot.py returned a same-session Stage 4 / AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN evaluation, so company technicals are available, but market-wide breadth and sector Stage 2 context are not. The scanner's minimum market capitalisation of ₹1,000 crore would also exclude SoftTech, so the TheWrap leaderboard field in the snapshot is not informative for this name.

The benchmark Nifty 50 daily bar for 13 November 2026 was not yet published when market_facts.py was run (one retry), so the verified session date is 12 November 2026, per the run protocol's data-availability fallback. The TradingView read used in Chapters 7 and 8 was taken after the 13 November session and includes a provisional last print of ₹425.90 on 816 shares; slopes, volumes and turnover are computed from NSE closes through 12 November.

The Q2 FY2027 earnings call was held on 13 November 2026, after the Q2 results. Its transcript could not be retrieved (access denied), so Q2 commentary is drawn from the filed results and the 6 November 2026 investor presentation [10][30]. The June 2026 call was the company's first earnings call, so the walk-the-talk audit in Chapter 5 relies on presentations and annual reports for earlier years.

The stock_snapshot.py valuation label ('Reasonable / In-line') and the options_snapshot.py setup text ('4H momentum turning up', 'above 4H EMA20') conflict with the same snapshot's numbers (P/E 118.9x with ROE 2.9%; price ₹425.90 below the 4H EMA20 of ₹431.01). The report relies on the numbers, not the labels, and the options_snapshot business-quality field was a default and is overridden by this report's CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL verdict.

technical_spec.intro_prose: We read SoftTech's tape at two dates, and you should keep them apart. The market-facts ledger is dated to the verified 12 November 2026 close of ₹420.95. The TradingView read was taken after the 13 November session, when the last print was ₹425.90 on 816 shares; slopes and volume tallies in the chapter text are my own calculations from NSE closes [41][42].
technical_spec.gate_intro_prose: Two of our screens classify the same chart differently, Stage 3 in the market-facts ledger and Stage 4 in the stock snapshot. We apply the stricter one to timing, and the table shows both.
technical_spec.closing_prose: The stricter timing rule and the valuation test in Chapters 7 and 9 both say no new capital. The support band in the table above works as a measuring stick for risk and reward, not a place to buy.
technical_spec.tech_table_takeaway: The first rows come from the market-facts ledger at the 12 November close; the weekly averages, pivots, rating and extensions come from TradingView after the 13 November session. The differences are small and are explained in Chapter 8.
technical_spec.gate_table_takeaway: Trend, timing and valuation are separate tests. SoftTech's chart is a pullback inside a rising long-term trend, but the timing gate is CAP_REJECTED and the valuation test fails.
technical_spec.stage_explanation: Price is below its 20- and 50-day averages and the 50-day average has flattened, while the 200-day and weekly 30-week averages are still rising. This is a pullback after a volume climax in September, not a broken trend.
technical_spec.evaluation_stage_explanation: The ledger's rules read the pullback below the 50-day average as Stage 3; the snapshot's rules, which test price against the 30-week average, read Stage 4. The 30-week average is still rising, so Stage 3 describes the chart better.
technical_spec.posture_explanation: The snapshot rule blocks new entries while price sits below both the 30-week and 50-day averages and says to wait for a Stage 1 base and a Stage 2 breakout.
technical_spec.support_zone_explanation: Reference band from pivot support and the 200-day average. At the top of the band the base-case value of ₹299 is below the price, so the band does not offer 1.5:1 reward-to-risk and is not a buy zone.
technical_spec.stop_placement_explanation: Pipeline reference level below the support band less 0.5 times ATR14. It is not an active stop, because no position is authorised.

valuation_assessment.posture: Rich (analyst override of the screen's 'Reasonable / In-line')
valuation_assessment.note: The screen compares the P/E with growth and ignores return on equity. At 119x trailing earnings with a 2.9% ROE and a reverse DCF that needs 29-35% revenue growth for five years, we judge the price rich (Chapter 7).
